questions.say: Good evening. My name is Emma, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your home. Can you describe your home?

questions.text: How long have you lived in your current home?
questions.say: How long have you lived in your current home?

questions.text: Do you know your neighbours well?
questions.say: Do you know your neighbours well?

questions.text: What is the best thing about the area where you live?
questions.say: What is the best thing about the area where you live?

questions.text: Do you read newspapers or magazines?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about newspapers and magazines. Do you read newspapers or magazines?

questions.text: Did your parents read newspapers when you were young?
questions.say: Did your parents read newspapers when you were young?

questions.text: Do you think newspapers will still exist in the future?
questions.say: Do you think newspapers will still exist in the future?

questions.text: Do you make a lot of phone calls?

questions.text: Who do you call most often?

questions.text: Do you prefer to call or to send a message?
questions.say: Do you prefer to call or to send a message?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you received some good news.
cueCard.explain: and explain how you felt when you heard it.

questions.text: Describe a time when you received some good news.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a time when you received some good news. You should say: what the news was; when you received it; how you received it; and explain how you felt when you heard it.

questions.text: Who did you share the news with first?
questions.say: Thank you. Who did you share the news with first?

questions.text: Why do newspapers and television report more bad news than good news?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a time when you received good news, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all news and the media. Why do newspapers and television report more bad news than good news?

questions.text: How do young people in your country get their news?
questions.say: How do young people in your country get their news?

questions.text: Is it better to share good news in person or online?
questions.say: Now let's talk about sharing news. Is it better to share good news in person or online?

questions.text: Why do people sometimes share news that is not true?
questions.say: Why do people sometimes share news that is not true?

questions.text: How has the speed at which news travels changed people's lives?
questions.say: How has the speed at which news travels changed people's lives?
